why: Telemetry for the queue-watermark case: two metric series and, for the first time in this corpus, a log line. The log is the broker's own warning, quoted verbatim from the incident text -- `logs show the disk watermark crossed 92 percent` -- because a log body this repository invented would be a sentence nobody wrote, and the guard holds every log body to a quote the same way it holds each layer's prose. What a log series adds that a metric cannot: RE2 and RE3 write a `logs.csv`, and until this case every one of those files in an export of this corpus had a header and no rows.

series.why: the checkpoint `cp-watermark` holds the post-onset value, and the text states the threshold it crossed
the checkpoint `cp-buffer` holds the post-onset value; the buffer grew because publishes were throttled rather than failed

logs.body: disk watermark crossed 92 percent; producers throttled
logs.why: the broker's own line, which is what makes this case's `logs.csv` a file with a row in it
